Ipsen Biopharm Ltd

Supported by nearly 100 years of development experience, with global hubs in the U.S., France and the U.K, we tackle areas of high unmet medical need through research and innovation.
Our passionate teams in more than 40 countries are focused on what matters and endeavor every day to bring medicines to patients in 88 countries. We build a workplace that champions human-centric leadership and fosters a culture of collaboration, excellence and impact. At Ipsen, every individual is empowered to be their true selves, grow and thrive alongside the company’s success. Join us on our journey towards sustainable growth, creating real impact on patients and society!

He/she drives excellence in external stakeholder management and leads the clinical partnerships for the programs and studies in scope, ensuring that Ipsen is seen as a partner of choice for external stakeholders and that any issues are addressed in a timely manner
The CPD is responsible for the clinical development plan and leads all clinical development operations aspects for the assets in scope at Asset Team level, ensuring cross-functional oversight of all program and study related activities
The CPD leverages market/industry insights to drive innovation and shape the company processes and programs to increase efficiency and collaboration
CPD could manage 1-2 program or multiple indications in a program

Accountable for forecasting/managing resources and for driving one-team, transparency, accountability and collaboration behaviors within his/her team and transversally within the organisation:

Fosters a culture of collaboration, accountability, continues improvement, and operational excellence

Contributes as required to advisory boards, expert scientific committees, and on submission teams
Brings in the industry insights into Ipsen to ensure we are building the organization to the future state
Analyse and recommend solutions to his/her line manager and other Heads of Department within CDO and R&D on the organisation and participation in effective clinical trial programs.
Drives changes in processes for continuous improvement, trainings and adaptation to business model changes.
Ensures all program activities within the framework are in compliance with Global SOPs, and other documentation in force within the Ipsen Group, ensuring timely reading and understanding of relevant SOPs.
Performs any other activity as may reasonably be required by his/her line manager from time to time

Drive Vision and Strategy

The CPD is responsible for the clinical development plan and leads all clinical development operations aspects for the assets in scope at Asset Team level.
Leverages market/industry insights to drive innovation and shape the company processes and programs to increase efficiency and collaboration.
CPD could manage 1-2 program or multiple indications in a program.
Ensures Accountability

About Realty Income
Realty Income (NYSE: O), an S&P 500 company, is a real estate partner to the world's leading companies. Founded in 1969, we invest in diversified commercial real estate and have a portfolio of 15,600 properties in all 50 U.S. states, the UK and six other countries in Europe, with a gross book value $58bn. We are known as "The Monthly Dividend Company®” and have a mission to deliver stockholders dependable monthly dividends that grow over time. Since our founding, we have declared 656 consecutive monthly dividends and are a member of the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats® index, having increased our dividend for the last 30 consecutive years.
You will be joining one of the largest Real Estate Investment Trusts in the world as we rapidly expand into the UK and European markets, including moving into new offices at 3 St. James’s Square.
The European portfolio, including the UK, has experienced consistent growth quarter-on-quarter since our first international acquisition, a £429m 12-property portfolio from Sainsbury’s in 2019. In just five years the portfolio now includes investments of over $11bn, and 483 distinct properties.
Position Overview
Realty Income is seeking a Director, Financial Reporting to provide specialist leadership across European financial close and consolidation, statutory and external reporting, technical accounting, audit management, SOX and internal controls, and joint venture reporting and governance. Based in London, this role will safeguard the integrity, consistency and compliance of reporting across multiple entities, jurisdictions and reporting frameworks. The Director will partner with senior finance, business, audit and joint venture stakeholders while driving standardisation, audit readiness, automation and continuous improvement across the European reporting environment.
Responsibilities
• Lead the monthly, quarterly and annual financial close across multiple European entities, ensuring timely, accurate and compliant reporting.
• Oversee multi-entity and multi-currency consolidation, including intercompany reconciliations, eliminations and consolidation adjustments.
• Review and approve material accounting entries, balance-sheet reconciliations and reporting adjustments, resolving complex close matters.
• Own the quality, completeness and timely delivery of group, statutory and external reporting across the European portfolio.
• Ensure compliance with IFRS, US GAAP, Dutch GAAP, Luxembourg GAAP and corporate accounting policies.
• Oversee preparation and filing of statutory financial statements and related regulatory reporting, maintaining consistent review and approval standards.
• Act as the European subject-matter expert on accounting frameworks and assess complex transactions including acquisitions, disposals, joint ventures, financing arrangements and restructurings.
• Lead implementation of new accounting standards and regulatory requirements and communicate clear technical guidance to finance, business and executive stakeholders.
• Lead European external audits, coordinating planning, information requests, issue resolution, statutory deliverables, regulatory filings and remediation of findings.
• Own key SOX controls for close, consolidation, reconciliations, intercompany, reporting and service-provider oversight, including walkthroughs, testing, deficiency assessment and management certification.
• Lead the joint venture reporting and governance framework, including partner reporting, ownership allocations, capital calls, distributions and reporting implications of transactions and restructurings.
• Drive reporting transformation, automation and process standardisation while overseeing deliverables from internal teams and third-party providers.
• Coach and develop finance team members and communicate significant accounting judgements, reporting risks, control matters and required actions to senior stakeholders.
Qualifications
We would expect the successful candidate to have:
• Significant progressive experience in financial reporting, technical accounting, audit or controllership within a complex multi-entity environment.
• Demonstrable expertise in IFRS and Dutch GAAP, with the judgement to assess and document complex and non-routine transactions.
• Experience leading multi-entity and multi-currency close and consolidation, statutory reporting and external audits.
• Experience owning SOX or an equivalent internal-control programme, including control design, evidence, deficiency assessment and remediation.
• Strong systems capability, including advanced Excel and experience with ERP, consolidation, reporting or property-management platforms.
• High integrity, sound judgement and clear ownership of financial-reporting quality.
• Credible senior communication skills, with the ability to challenge constructively and influence across a matrixed organisation.
• Strong technical, analytical and problem-solving capability, with attention to detail and broader business awareness.
• A collaborative leadership style, continuous-improvement mindset and ability to manage competing priorities across jurisdictions.
• A qualified accountant designation: ACA, ACCA, CPA, CIMA or equivalent, with a minimum of five years post-qualified experience.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with US GAAP and additional European reporting frameworks.
• Pan-European real estate, REIT or investment-management experience.
• Big Four audit, accounting-advisory or technical-accounting experience.
• Experience leading joint venture reporting, partner governance, capital calls, distributions and ownership allocations.
• A record of delivering reporting transformation, automation, process standardisation and stronger control effectiveness.

Our Mission & Values
For more than 50 years, Realty Income has been guided by our mission to invest in people and places to deliver dependable monthly dividends that increase over time. We do this by nurturing long-term, meaningful relationships that enable people to achieve a better financial outlook. We understand that when individuals succeed financially, they are able to provide for their families, support local businesses and pursue their greatest ambitions, creating a lasting positive impact on communities.

Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something extraordinary - shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical or business professionals, and as such we will also support you through your preferred route for professional development. The role requires an enthusiastic individual who has a passion for overcoming technical challenges.
We are looking for a graduate to do Stress and Thermal Analysis within the Mechanical Engineering Team —shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
Our 18-month Graduate Programmes give you the opportunity to work on exciting and challenging projects alongside industry leaders.
On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum, plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria.
We encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.
During the programme, as a Graduate Engineer - Stress amd Thermal Analyst, you will
• Support the design and development of our world leading electro-optic, communications and information systems products under the guidance of experienced mechanical engineers.
• Be introduced to state-of-the-art methods, technology and tools to enable you to explore all aspects of the engineering lifecycle, including requirements analysis, design, implementation, test, build, production and in-service support.
This role allows a mixture of on-site and remote working; with attendance at our Essex facility required when Customer requirements dictate.
Key Responsibility Areas
Acquiring the skills required to work effectively within a professional engineering environment. Analysing and advising on thermal and stress performance to help products meet demanding environmental and operational requirements.
Supporting members of the mechanical engineering team in the delivery of technical solutions that meet our customer needs. Design and develop structures of products providing information about the behaviour of a structure, related to its static and dynamic response supporting both new innovations and proven legacy products.
•
• Creating and presenting design data to the appropriate departmental ‘best practices’ and utilising industry leading tool sets.
• Delivering detailed designs, including numerical calculations, tolerance studies, etc.
• Working to meet cost, schedule and quality demands.
What you will bring
All of our roles require (a) a minimum of a 2:2 Bachelors/Integrated Master’s degree, or (b) a higher degree, such as a MSc or PhD.
For the Graduate Stress and Thermal Engineer role, the acceptable degrees are:
•
• Mechanical Engineering
• Aero-Mechanical Engineering
• Mechatronics
• Electro Mechanical
Personal Attributes
•
• Be a self-motivated individual, willing to take on new challenges and drive continuous personal development.
• Strong communication skills across a variety of mediums i.e. written, verbal, digital, etc.
• The ability to develop effective working relationships with peers and stakeholders.
• Adaptable to the ever-changing demands that will be encountered within the role.
• Offer novel ideas and methods for solving complex problems, drawing on personal experiences and knowledge learned during academic studies.
• Demonstrate relevant project work and/or placements in Industry are beneficial, but not essential.
What you’ll do
• Analyse and assess mechanical designs for strength, durability, performance and safety against regulatory and customer requirements using finite element techniques and classical hand calculations.
• Conduct thermal analysis of mechanical designs to assess performance and safety using thermal analysis software, CFD techniques, and classical hand calculations.
• Support the selection of manufacturing technologies and aerospace materials based on a sound understanding of material physical and mechanical properties and the mechanical fit, form and function of the product.
• Advise on materials and manufacturing techniques with an emphasis on thermal performance and mechanical integrity.
• Support product development through all phases—from design and testing to final certification.
• Contribute to technical documentation, including material for peer reviews and stage/gate approvals.
• All members of the Analysis Team are encouraged and supported to continually develop their skills, including (but not limited to) Structural, Thermal, Pressure and Model Driven domains.
Desirable
• Working evidence on the application of a wide range of classical hand calculation techniques for static and dynamic loading conditions and fatigue assessment (Land, Naval or Airborne equipment).
• Experience of manufacturing and joining techniques, engineering material properties.
• Experience of environmental test methods for design verification and working knowledge of design certification for land based and airborne equipment.
• Awareness of equipment safety compliance requirements, including the ability to support inspection processes and generate fault and failure reports.
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

Job Description:
Private Assurance -Experienced Technician, Milton Keynes or Manchester
NEW GROUND WON’T BREAK ITSELF.
Every day, our teams help individuals, businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals.
The Private Assurance Team works with a huge variety of ultra-high net worth individuals, ensuring their personal tax compliance obligations are met. We build trusted long-term relationships with clients, taking the time to understand their needs and building an understanding of their financial affairs providing a bespoke service to help them achieve their goals.
We are committed to continual improvement, refining our internal processes, embracing new technology to support us in the way we collaborate and communicate with our clients.
We recognise the importance of achieving a balance between work and personal life. That’s why we are happy to discuss and support flexible working arrangements.
A look into the role
As an experienced technician within our Private Assurance team:
• You will be trusted with a degree of autonomy in delivering your work, empowering you to take initiative and apply your judgement whilst knowing dedicated support is available.
• You will oversee a portfolio of complex clients, handling complex tax returns and projects. You will take full ownership of your client portfolio and proactively manage the entire tax return process from start to finish, with support and guidance from your manager.
• You will prepare tax returns and computations for manager review. Using your initiative to conduct well-supported technical research applying relevant legislation, tax authoritative guidance, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) manuals and the firm’s resources to effectively generate an opinion.
• You will engage directly with clients and HMRC, developing relationships built on trust, accuracy, and responsiveness. You will provide clear, timely communication and become a reliable point of contact for day-to-day tax matters.
• You will take responsibility for driving the tax return process for your clients, proactively managing deadlines, organising and prioritising day to day tasks and considering Work in Progress management/recoveries on assignments.
• You will contribute to a culture of collaboration becoming a valued and proactive member of a specialised team. Developing and building strong internal relationships by networking within the tax service line and other service lines, gaining insights and sharing knowledge to enhance overall service delivery.
• This role is key to the operation of our private tax function, contributing to Private Assurance’s wider goals whilst maintaining professional excellence. As part of this, you will be supported with structured learning opportunities, on-the-job coaching, and exposure to varied work that will accelerate your technical and personal development.
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as a Tax Executive, the minimum criteria you’ll need is experience in UK Personal Tax, A-Levels or equivalent, good grades in Maths and English GCSE, and excellent written and verbal communication skills. It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
• ATT qualification (or working towards) – study support is available
• Self-motivated and driven
• Highly organised with an ability to work to deadlines and manage expectations
Knowing we’re right for you
The culture at Grant Thornton is what sets us apart, we’re known for our inclusive culture and creating environments where all our people can flourish. The things that set you apart, we value them, and this helps us all to perform at our best.
Our values are the unwavering principles that shape our daily behaviours and decisions, alongside our drive to do the right thing. We’re looking for people who align with our values and are purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind. You can learn more about our values in practice here.
It’s not just about our culture and values, in addition to a competitive salary and reward package, us you’ll also get:
• Tailored development programmes and access to coaching
• Flexible bank holidays – allowing you to celebrate the days that are important to you
• Benefits including pension, life assurance and private medical, additional holiday purchasing and health benefits
• Any benefits giving you access to shopping discounts, gym memberships, financial advice
And more. Visit our benefits section to read more.
How we work
We have a trust-based way of working, driven by responsible people who have the best interests of our firm and our clients at heart. Our how we work framework gives flexibility in where, how, and when we work to deliver the best results for our clients, whilst helping you keep a balance between work and life. Life is more than work, the things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles.  That is how it should be.
We’re looking for people who can help drive the business forward, who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what’s right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It’s how it should be.

Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.

Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
•
Customer-focused approach with the ability to build trusted client relationships.
•
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Confident and resilient when handling complex or challenging claims.
•

GCSE Maths and English (or equivalent).
•
A Levels (desirable).

Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new

We invite you to grow your career with us, experience our caring culture, and enjoy work-life balance. Here, there’s no limit to what you can achieve.
Claims Technician - Domestic Major Loss - North England
Be the calm voice claimants rely on to get their lives back on track.
Job Location: North England
Job Type: Permanent
Remuneration: Competitive salary taking into account skills, experience and qualifications
We have a fantastic opportunity for Adjusting Executives in the North of England
The Claims Technician (known internally as Adjusting Executive) is a technical assistant role, designed to support the Loss Adjuster throughout the handling of the claims. You'll be the first point of contact, guiding customers through the claims process. Each day brings a new puzzle: deciphering details, recommending settlements, and collaborating with contractors to get things fixed. The role requires both empathy and initiative – clear communication helps customer’s feel supported, while independent thinking keeps claims moving forward.
Imagine being the calming voice after a homeowner discovers water flowing into their property following floods. You’ll explain complex details to relieved claimants and have contractors praising your organisational skills. It's a chance to make a real difference in people's lives, one steady step at a time.
Whether working from home or in our bright, collaborative office, you'll be part of a supportive team. We offer comprehensive training to develop your skills, and the chance to earn a prestigious industry qualification (Chartered Institute of Loss Adjusters' Cert CILA).
It's a perfect fit for those who crave variety, enjoy problem-solving, and want to build a rewarding career in a fast-paced environment.
The skills you will have when you apply:
•
Experience in managing property claims: Previous experience in a claims environment is essential.
•
Excellent communication skills: You'll speak with and write to policyholders, insurers, contractors, and more. You’ll explain complex details clearly, and negotiate fair settlements for all.
•
Conscientious and hard working in order to achieve the required results, as well as being flexible and adaptable during times of high volumes
The skills that will be developed once working:
•
Comprehensive Training: You'll receive all the Sedgwick-specific training needed to excel in your role.
•
Professional Development: We are committed to helping you work towards the Chartered Institute of Loss Adjusters' Cert CILA qualification.
What we’ll give you for this role:
Remuneration & more
•
Competitive salary taking into account skills, experience and qualifications
•
A Self Invested Personal Pension Scheme (SIPP)
•
Holiday allowance of 25 days plus bank holidays
•
Flexible working from our office or your home
Health & support
•
Private healthcare plan (including pre-existing conditions)
•
Life assurance
•
Employee assistance programme for employee wellbeing
•
Group Income Protection
Other benefits
•
Voluntary flexible benefits – green car scheme, travel insurance, dental cover, cycle to work scheme, season ticket loan, wellbeing and digital GP applications
•
Discounts on various products and services
This isn't just a position, it's a pivotal role in shaping our industry
At Sedgwick, not only will you be working behind the scenes for some of the UK's most trusted insurance brands helping to resolve millions of claims every year, you'll also be an architect of tomorrow's insurance landscape with Sedgwick University. Our proprietary offering is the most comprehensive training and development program in the industry with more than 15,000 courses on demand, training specific to roles, and opportunities to continue your formal education – all available to you starting from your very first day.
You'll join a community passionate about making a difference, where every role contributes to a larger mission; protecting people and businesses. This isn't just a job; it's an opportunity to shape the future of insurance.

Join Anglian Water's Strategic Pipeline Alliance as a Land Consultant.
Location:                    Flexible / Hybrid from office or home, with site visits across the region as and when required
Employment Type:   Full-time, Permanent
Are you detail-oriented, organized, and passionate about contributing to one of the UK’s most ambitious water infrastructure projects? The Strategic Pipeline Alliance (SPA) is searching for a Land Consultant to support and enhance our project delivery team.
What will you be doing as our new Land Consultant.
The Strategic Pipeline Alliance (SPA) is a ~£1.8Bn framework delivering 500km+ of transfer pipelines, with associated storage and pumping assets, across the East of England supporting reduction of abstraction in sensitive aquifers and significant regional growth.
You will play a key role in the successful delivery of the SPA project being part of the Land team reporting to the Land Programme Manager, undertaking key land referencing activities in line with the Water Industry Act 1991.
Key responsibilities:
• Lead on Identifying legal interests in land; including freeholders, leaseholders, tenants and rights by researching and compiling land ownership records using HMLR, Local authority and other such methods
• Batching and mailing out land entry questionnaires to confirm ownership and agreement to access land
• Processing returned questionnaires and ensuring that the land management system is updated with confirmed information
• Carry out site visits to confirm land ownership / interest details etc.
• Work with GIS / GIS resource to ensure that landownership extents are correctly captured on the GIS platform
• Manage and request land access for surveys (non-intrusive and intrusive), to support EIA requirements, and construction activities:
• Work with relevant disciplines to understand access requirements and ensure that requests are made and obtained in line with the survey request timescales and processes
• Support access requirements at later stages with management of landowner consultation:
• Provide support to the agricultural liaison officers during the construction phase, assisting in resolving any identified risks or landowner concerns
A little bit about your skills, experience and behaviours:
This job might be for you if you:
• Have experience of being part of a large-scale infrastructure programme, in particular ones that have an impact on agricultural businesses.
• Have experience using project systems to record stakeholder interactions and project progress
• You enjoy research and investigation to identify the relevant interest in a land parcel
• You enjoy working collaboratively as part of a team, and are able to work independently where required
• You are an engaging and enthusiastic individual that can form relationships at ease and is an excellent communicator who can build and sustain relationships with the project teams and external stakeholders
• You are willing to travel and be located at the scheme location when required to carry out site visits in line with the referencing exercises.
Not only do we look for the best talent to join us on our journey, we also look for individuals to demonstrate key behaviours that align with our values and beliefs.
Working with the highest degree of integrity, we want SPA employees to take ownership and accountability for their outputs and be driven to continuously improve how they work. SPA employees should act with the customer’s best interest at heart, be clear and transparent communicators and be passionate about operating in an ethical fashion.
If you are looking for a career opportunity, working in an innovative forward-thinking environment please apply today!
Why Join SPA?
The Strategic Pipeline Alliance Project is at the exciting delivery stage, with additional projects lined up for AMP8. At SPA, we embrace innovation, digital technology, and collaboration with our partners, including Farrans, MMB, Costain, and Jacobs.
Together, we’re combating climate change and securing clean water for generations to come.
• Flexible Working: We support remote working, part-time hours, and flexible schedules to suit your lifestyle if the role allows.
• Location: Our office is in Peterborough, with operational hubs across the project area.  This role is predominantly site based.
• Diversity and Inclusion: SPA is committed to building an inclusive, welcoming environment for everyone. Whatever your background, if this role resonates with you, we encourage you to apply.
Our Purpose
Our mission is simple yet vital: To Make the East of England Resilient to the Effects of Drought. Join us in shaping a sustainable future while being part of a team where everyone can thrive.
Ready to Join Us?
If you’re passionate about making a meaningful impact and excited to lead in a transformative environment, we’d love to hear from you!
SPA is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and recruit based on merit and potential, ensuring every colleague feels a sense of belonging.
Take the Next Step
If you’re passionate about delivering innovative infrastructure solutions and want to make a difference, we’d love to hear from you.
Apply now and be part of Anglian Water’s journey to build a more sustainable, water-secure future.

Evolito’s mission is to accelerate the adoption of electric propulsion in aerospace applications in support of a net-zero world.  We will help to revolutionise personal mobility and transform our towns and cities with clean, noise-free air transportation.
Evolito develops and manufactures class-leading, lightweight, high-power, and high-torque-density electric propulsion systems for a range of aerospace markets, including EVTOL, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and General Aviation.
As well as ultra-high performance, low-weight electric motors and controllers, Evolito specialises in high-integrity, bespoke battery systems for the aerospace and defence markets. The team is scaling rapidly and has ambitious growth plans over the next twelve to eighteen months.
As part of our current high‑growth phase, we are seeking a Senior Fatigue & Damage Tolerance Analysis Engineer to join the team to ensure lead the development and deployment of fatigue and damage tolerance (F&DT) analysis methods for metallic and composite structures, both rotating and static components, for electric propulsion architecture including the motor.
Key responsibilities will include:
•
Carry out detailed fatigue and crack growth analysis using both first‑principles and industry recognised analysis/calculation methods
•
Analyse the life of rotating metallic (aluminium, steel and titanium) components consistent with Group A critical parts
•
Assess results against customer specifications and draw sound conclusions, including the generation of LCF, Damage Tolerance and Residual Fatigue
•
Determination of fatigue allowable stress levels for sizing
•
Determination of inspection intervals for structural parts consistent with CS25 requirements
•
Collaborate closely with Design, Test and Airworthiness teams to integrate F&DT solutions into the certification programmes
•
Author technical documentation to support regulatory submissions
•
Develop ideas and design solutions to practical challenges arising from new product design
•
Drive and manage test work that will validate the analysis
•
Support DFMEAs, other quality techniques and complete actions required to mitigate risks
•
Write specifications and reports as required through the product lifecycle, utilising a structured approach to problem-solving techniques.
​
Skills and experience required:
•
Proven experience in evaluation of static and rotating components, specifically CS25 level lifing compliance with respect to LCF, Damage Tolerance and Residual Fatigue
•
Proven experience of Critical Parts lifing for LCF, Damage Tolerance and Residual Fatigue (Deterministic and Probabilistic)
•
Calculation of equivalent (Seq) stresses (fatigue and crack propagation), understanding of mission profiles, rainflow counting, Miner's rule and F&DT databases
•
Analysis of metallic and composite structures (Plain Strength checks, Buckling, Bolted joint analysis)
•
Knowledge of static and fatigue design values (Ftu, Fty, Fcy, AFI parameters, S-N curve parameters, fracture toughness, etc)
•
Possess a strong foundation in the area of load/stress analysis with abilities to formulate "free body diagrams" and identify load path of structures
•
Practical knowledge of electric machines or rotating assemblies
•
Strong experience with FEA methods and programs e.g. ANSYS (ideally).
•
Self-sufficient and able to work with minimal managerial input
•
Good understanding of aerospace materials and associated mechanical properties and processing
•
Confident with customers and suppliers, able to interpret requirements and understand issues
•
A flexible approach to work with the desire to thrive in a dynamic, fast-moving environment
•
Strong communication skills (both written and verbal), good collaboration skills, and the ability to work effectively across teams
•
Self-motivated with the determination to succeed.
​
Desirable:
•
Experience in aerospace certification programmes
•
Experience with polymers-creep evaluation.

In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Graduate Radio Frequency (RF) Engineer
This role will be based in Celtic Lakes. Our new 237,000-square-foot Newport facility provides additional production and customer collaboration spaces, including 25,000 square feet of R&D clean rooms, 35,000 square feet of innovative manufacturing space and tool demo areas, all designed to support development of semiconductor process technologies across advanced packaging, power devices, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), radio frequency (RF) and photonics sector technology!
You’ll be joining one of our product design teams covering either our CVD, PVD, or Etch products, providing electrical & electronic solutions from our head office in Newport.
This role is part of our 2027 Graduate programme and will start in September 2027.

Following our extensive onboarding and introduction program, you will join our Graduate Development program which includes Technical Classroom training, Soft-skills training, Team building, corporate responsibility activities and finally placement across all our operations and process and design teams.

• Design and construction of prototype electronics and RF hardware including
• RF plasma delivery systems generators
• Matching units,
• RF matching unit circuitry,
• networks, transformers, filters, RF electrode circuitry, isolation and filter circuits
• DC bias handling, PCB design package.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here
PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.
About AI for Health
PATH’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative is our flagship technical team working across divisions to deliver best-in-class evaluation and implementation of AI in health, spanning model evaluation to product development and service innovation. We aim to use AI to address the world’s largest health inequities.
We’re looking for an early career researcher to help deliver a multi-country programme evaluating whether AI can provide safe and effective mental health/wellbeing support for those most in need. You will contribute to research to test and improve how automated evaluation methods (e.g., patient simulation, LLM-judging) reflect people and languages in different settings, and to make effective use of local clinicians and lived experience input.
A key part of the role will be undertaking a fully-funded PhD (supervised by PATH’s Chief AI Officer and Professor at University College London, Dr. Bilal Mateen, and co-supervised by the relevant technical leadership at PATH and UCL), investigating how we can most effectively and efficiently use human expertise and local data to deliver accurate and localised evaluation of AI performance across different languages and contexts.
The role is a strong fit for an evaluation science or computational researcher who wants to shape how AI is assessed across settings and earn a PhD through that work as a route into AI safety and global (mental) health.
Responsibilities:
There won’t be a typical day in this role. You could be doing anything from drafting a protocol for a new study to organising a consensus workshop with partners from around the world or running in-silico experiments and analysing data generated by our partners. If you thrive on tinkering with tools, independently playing around with a task/problem, and having a team that supports you in failing fast and learning a lot, then this is the role for you. Support Research Delivery and Operations across the Programme
We’ll carve out a specific set of partners and tasks (aligned with your PhD topic) whom you will be the primary point of contact for, spanning operational and technical needs (as summarised below). Your job will be to make sure those elements of the grant-funded projects we’re collaborating on with our partners happen as planned.
• Support the AI for Health team’s research agenda: contribute technical input as the team and its partners design, run, and analyse evaluation studies, including developing and testing simulated users/patients and LLM-judges and running evaluations of AI models and products.
• Work with the Deputy Director of Operations and Finance and their team on the operational, administrative, and project management components of research delivery, including ethics and governance submissions, partner reporting, and workplan tracking.
Develop Your Research Skills
• Complete a fully funded PhD at University College London as the core vehicle for developing your research skills. Under the guidance of your supervisors, conceive, design, and carry out the studies that make up your thesis, which will address how human expertise and local data can most effectively and efficiently be used to deliver accurate and localised evaluation of AI performance across different languages and contexts. Topics could include:
• Analysing what clinicians and lived experience experts in different countries consider to be helpful and harmful AI behaviour: what is shared between contexts, what is local to individual settings, how much different experts agree/disagree, and how plurality of opinion can be represented in our evaluations.
• Developing and adapting automated evaluation methods to reflect how people in each setting talk about their mental health and seek support from AI, including in local languages and where people mix languages.
• Studying how to make the most of scarce expert time and local data: which ways of collecting expert feedback and data improve our evaluation tools most efficiently, and how much ongoing human input we need to stay reliable.
• Contribute to studies led by other members of the AI for Health team, and to the development of the team’s wider research agenda, whilst building your own methodological and technical skills over the course of the post, with the support of your supervisors.
This is a full-time post based in London, combining research delivery at PATH with registration for a PhD at University College London, fully funded for three years. You’ll report to PATH’s Deputy Director for AI for Health, and your PhD will be jointly supervised by leadership at PATH and UCL. The role includes occasional international travel to partner sites (around 5-10% of time).
Required Skills and Experience:
• MSc or BSc in data science, psychology, cognitive science, statistics, computer science, human–computer interaction, computational linguistics, epidemiology, or a related quantitative discipline.

Oracle Cloud ERP Finance Technical Consultant
Career level: Consultant / Associate Manager (CL9–CL8)  |  Location: London / Manchester / Edinburgh  |  Practice: Finance Reinvention Partner (Oracle)
Why this role
This role builds the Oracle Cloud finance solutions our clients run their books on. You'll take a finance design and turn it into a working, tested, migrated system that stands up at go-live and holds together afterwards. That means the configuration, the build specifications, the integrations and the data conversion behind them, and the evidence that it all works. You'll do it on large-scale Oracle Cloud ERP finance transformations, with real ownership of your own scope: a workstream lead sets the direction and owns the design authority, while you own the build within it and the technical decisions that come with it.
You'll do that work from inside the client's finance function, in their design sessions, alongside their controllers and their IT team. You'll explain why the system behaves the way it does to people who will never open a configuration screen, hold a design decision when it is challenged, and become the person a client comes back to when the answer has to be right. We're hiring for both halves of that: the technical depth, and the judgement to carry it in front of a client.
Accenture is a leading solutions and services company. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI. We bring together our people, deep industry expertise and technology to deliver end-to-end outcomes for clients — and Finance is one of seven Reinvention Partners at the centre of that. Finance RP brings the CFO agenda to life for clients — stronger performance, sharper insight, and better control.
"Our clients want a partner that can help them reinvent—boldly, continuously and at speed… while continuously building the most client-focused, AI-enabled great place to work for our people—our Reinventors." — Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO
What you'll bring
Oracle Cloud configuration depth. Hands-on configuration of Oracle Cloud ERP Financials (Oracle Fusion Cloud Financials) across the core finance modules: General Ledger, Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets, Cash Management, Tax and Intercompany, plus the enterprise and ledger structures underneath them. You configure it, you test it, and you can stand behind why it is set up the way it is. That extends into Oracle Subledger Accounting, where you understand how transactions are accounted and how to configure the rules that decide it; consolidation and close in FCCS; and enterprise data and chart-of-accounts structures in EDMCS. You stay on standard, extending Oracle the way it is designed to be extended rather than modifying it, and you can explain to a client why that boundary is worth holding. Experience across the wider Oracle finance estate, including the EPM suite and planning in EPBCS, broadens where you can work. The platform matters less than the rigour you bring, so comparable cloud finance platforms are worth talking to us about.
Design, build and integration. You translate finance requirements into functional designs and into build specifications a developer can work from, covering reports, interfaces, data conversions, extensions, workflow and integrations. You build the reporting yourself in BI Publisher, OTBI and Smart View, and you have worked hands-on with Oracle's integration patterns across Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) and REST and SOAP web services. Data migration and conversion sits with you, using FBDI and ADFdi, so a cutover holds. Where the standard product doesn't reach, you extend it properly, in a sandbox and through Visual Builder. You take the solution through testing and into deployment, and you know what evidence a client needs before they will sign it off.
Finance process knowledge. Genuine Record-to-Report depth, with a feel for how your configuration choices show up for the CFO: a faster close, numbers people trust, stronger control. You understand enterprise structures and chart-of-accounts design and the finance master data underneath them, how finance controls are built into the configuration rather than bolted on afterwards, and how those choices shape reporting downstream. Exposure to a second finance process area broadens your range.
Delivery and client skills. You own your scope and see it through. You make the configuration and design calls within it, document them, and explain them to the client and to the workstream lead without either needing to check your working line by line. You're at ease in front of a client: running a working session with finance and IT stakeholders, walking them through what you've built, taking the questions it raises, and turning a technical constraint into what it means for their close, their controls and their reporting. You are straight with people about what the system will and won't do, and you say so early, not late. You bring structured, analytical problem-solving and communicate clearly under pressure, and you support the people around you by reviewing a colleague's configuration, bringing someone newer through a build, and passing on what is worth reusing on the next programme.
Ways of working. We're increasingly an AI-first delivery team, bringing agentic tooling and orchestration into how we design, build, test and validate, with our people owning the judgement and the outcome. An appreciation of Oracle's own embedded Fusion AI and agents, and how they augment a finance solution, is a real plus, and we're keen to hear from people bringing that experience.
Who you are
You take ownership and follow through without being chased. You work well in a delivery team and build straightforward, trusted working relationships with client counterparts. You can explain a technical decision to someone who isn't technical: plainly, without talking down and without hiding behind the detail. You bring good judgement to ambiguous problems and you're careful and clear in how you make and explain technical decisions. You know which calls are yours and which belong to the workstream lead, and you raise the second kind early. You're precise about detail and thorough about proof. You test your own configuration and satisfy yourself it holds before you report it as complete.
Things that set strong candidates apart: Oracle certification; hands-on configuration experience on end-to-end Oracle Cloud ERP finance implementations, from early design through to go-live; depth in the Oracle finance suite, whether subledger accounting, consolidation (FCCS) or enterprise data (EDMCS); reporting build in BI Publisher or OTBI; integration and data-conversion experience on Oracle Cloud across Oracle Integration Cloud, REST and SOAP services and FBDI; an awareness of how controls, master data and staying on standard shape a finance solution; and a professional finance or accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or…

We own the SDLC languages (Java, Python, .NET, Rust, and Golang) used by the firm’s developers, both for organically grown and inorganically acquired applications.  We succeed by helping our customers succeed, so understanding their business and technical problems is key to accelerating their delivery and ensuring consistency for legally required areas like compliance.
You'll join a supportive team with a healthy mix of experience levels, working alongside Directors and a Technical Fellow who set a high bar for technical excellence. This is a team where you'll be mentored, challenged, and given real ownership from day one.
As a Java Developer, you will strengthen the firm’s Java language support and help develop the shared platform capabilities used by financial applications operating at significant scale. These capabilities include libraries, build systems, database failover libraries, and shared business libraries maintained in partnership with application teams.
Java is the firm’s most mature programming language, creating complex engineering challenges across performance, reliability, scale, and developer experience. You will help address these challenges while also contributing expert guidance to the wider programming-language community. Your work will support technology that helps investors pursue important financial goals, including saving for retirement, paying for education, purchasing a home, and improving their financial well-being.
Your responsibilities
In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following
responsibilities:
• Deliver practical engineering solutions within a complex operating environment, navigating multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
• Strengthen the Java SDLC by developing and maintaining shared libraries, build systems, database failover capabilities, and application-team-owned business libraries.
• Address demanding performance, resilience, scalability, and survivability requirements for applications operating at significant scale.
• Contribute to the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) development tooling and evaluate how emerging engineering practices can improve delivery.
• Provide expert guidance to the wider programming-language community and help improve the developer experience across the other languages supported by the team.
• Design, test, deploy, and support resilient systems while developing a strong understanding of how platform teams operate at scale.
• Collaborate with global engineering and application teams, share ideas, seek feedback, and contribute to a culture of continuous improvement.
Your experience
• Demonstrated software engineering experience and sound judgement gained through designing, delivering, and supporting production systems. Financial services experience is not required, and relevant practical experience is valued more than a specific degree.
• Strong Java programming experience and solid engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, version control, and writing clean, testable code.
• Demonstrated curiosity about how technologies work, with the motivation and adaptability to learn new programming languages, toolchains, and infrastructure.
• Interest in build systems, containers, and Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) practices, with a hands-on approach to learning by building and improving solutions. Previous experience in these areas is helpful but not essential.
• A collaborative, team-first approach, including following through on commitments, communicating openly, seeking feedback, and supporting colleagues.
• A proactive working style, with the ability to identify opportunities, raise issues early, and take ownership without waiting for detailed direction.
• Clear communication skills, with the ability to explain technical work and engineering decisions to technical and non-technical audiences and ask questions when requirements are unclear.
Our benefits
To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.
Our hybrid work model
BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.
Guidance on AI use for candidates
At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.
About BlackRock
At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being.  Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.

Location:

Our Mission
At Rolls-Royce SMR, we're delivering a new generation of low-carbon nuclear power that will help address the world's growing energy needs while supporting the transition to net zero. Through innovative engineering, advanced manufacturing and a relentless focus on safety, we're developing industry-leading Small Modular Reactor technology that will provide reliable, clean energy for generations to come.
The Team
You'll join our specialist Structural Integrity team within the Engineering function, working as part of the Component & Structural Integrity Integration capability. This is a highly influential team responsible for providing technical leadership, governance and assurance for the structural integrity of safety-critical pressure boundary components across the Rolls-Royce SMR power station.
Working alongside a small team of experienced specialists, you'll collaborate closely with design, materials, manufacturing, quality, non-destructive examination (NDE) and safety case teams. The team plays a critical role in supporting regulatory engagement, progressing the Generic Design Assessment (GDA) programme and ensuring the highest standards of nuclear safety are embedded throughout the design process.
The Role
This is a rare opportunity to become the recognised technical authority for Structural Integrity within one of the UK's most exciting nuclear programmes. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Component & Structural Integrity Integration, you'll provide strategic technical leadership across the business, ensuring robust structural integrity requirements are established and implemented across pressure boundary components.
You will lead the Structural Integrity aspects of the nuclear safety case, support key regulatory interactions and influence engineering decisions across multidisciplinary teams. The role offers significant visibility, allowing you to shape organisational capability, engage directly with regulators and contribute to the successful delivery of critical programme milestones.
What We’ll Need You to Do
• Lead the Structural Integrity elements of the nuclear safety case and support key regulatory submissions and assessments.
• Act as the technical authority for Structural Integrity, providing governance and expert guidance across the business.
• Support successful delivery of the Generic Design Assessment (GDA) programme and other critical engineering milestones.
• Define and embed Structural Integrity requirements across pressure boundary components including pressure vessels, piping and valves.
• Collaborate with design, materials, manufacturing, quality and NDE teams to ensure safe, compliant and efficient engineering solutions.
• Engage with regulators, external partners and suppliers, representing Rolls-Royce SMR on Structural Integrity matters.
• Mentor and influence engineers and specialists, helping to strengthen capability and promote a positive nuclear safety culture.
What You’ll Bring
• Degree, HND or equivalent qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering or a related technical discipline.
• Active progress towards, or attainment of, professional registration with a recognised engineering institution.
• Significant Structural Integrity experience within the nuclear industry or another highly regulated engineering environment.
• Strong understanding of pressure boundary components, including pressure vessels, piping systems and valves.
• Knowledge of Structural Integrity disciplines including design, stress analysis, materials, manufacturing, quality and non-destructive examination.
• Experience developing, presenting and defending safety cases and engaging with regulatory bodies.
• Working knowledge of ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code Section III and relevant industry standards, combined with excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Location
We offer flexible and hybrid working arrangements designed to support both collaboration and work-life balance. This role can be based from any Rolls-Royce SMR office location, with travel to Derby, Warrington and Manchester required to support project delivery, team

Alternatively, Grant Thornton
At Grant Thornton we do things differently - looking to the future, driving ambitious growth and pioneering positive change in our industry. Providing audit, tax and advisory services, we empower clients through strategic insight, curiosity, and genuine partnership. And we empower our people with real opportunity, an inclusive culture and work life balance. A true alternative.
With over 5,000 people in the UK, and a presence in 150 global markets, we're on an ambitious journey, from great to exceptional, and we need the best people to help us achieve our potential. And with that comes the opportunity to help redefine what our industry looks like, and what you want from your career.
Job Description:
Why Audit at Grant Thornton
Our UK audit practice is built of over 2300 people working across 24 locations, led by Wendy Russell and supported by 50 audit partners. We’re really proud of the strong position our audit practice is in from a wellbeing, resource and quality perspective, the latter of which is shown through our recent positive AQR results. Every day our teams help people in businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals. Our tailored and responsive approach provides the expertise our clients need, enabling them to grow and make the right decisions about their future.
Now’s the time to take everything you know about audit to the next level, with our growing portfolio of clients. The constantly evolving landscape calls for an approach that puts what is right first, ahead of what is easy, and you will need to push ideas harder and ask difficult questions, giving our clients the assurance, they need.
Our size and culture allow us to give you more opportunities within your career. You will have more responsibility for client outputs, and more variety in the work you take on and the clients you work with. You can develop your career in a way that works for you, and the firm, and we’ll support you with development programmes and opportunities along the way.
We’re keen to support and hire those who have had career breaks or time away from Audit in industry roles, who would like to return to a busy, flexible auditing role. Our vacancies for qualified Auditors are all open to supporting the up-skilling and re-integration of returners to our business.
A look into the role
We are looking for an CASS and Safeguarding Assistant Manager with external audit experience, including experience of Client Asset (CASS) audits and CASS safeguarding reviews, to support a growing client base in a market that is developing quickly.
Here are some things you can expect from this financial services role.
• You’ll consistently achieve deadlines and understand the commercial implications of actions relating to productivity, recoverability, fee income and client service.
•  You will be the key contact for the client on day-to-day matters and take the lead on dealing with large, technically complex clients. You’ll highlight all key issues which may affect the audit opinion to the partner and makes recommendations for appropriate action. Determining that all audit reports reflect the work performed, you will meet set reporting and auditing standards, acting as a point of reference for best practice.
• Regular communication and feedback must be provided whilst encouraging training and development for yourself and others.
• We will empower you to act as a trusted business adviser to our clients. You will take responsibility for managing key client portfolio and building and maintaining good working relationships with all colleagues and clients.
• Organising and attending office marketing events, you will be aware of the wide range of services the firm offers and suggest innovative products to address the clients' needs, following up on any contacts made. You’ll prepare and present proposals for new work whilst building a personal network from which referrals are received.
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as an Cass & Safeguarding Assistant Manager, you must have at least two years of experience managing statutory and CASS audits for financial services clients.
It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way:
• Experience of managing audits of large companies in addition to dealing with complex technical matters.
• Excellent knowledge of UK GAAP / FRS102.
• Project management experience.
• Experience of IFRS and auditing listed companies would be beneficial.
• Strong understanding of FCA CASS rules, including CASS safeguarding requirements and regulatory expectations.
• Experience conducting or supporting CASS safeguarding audits, assurance reviews, or related compliance engagements.
• Knowledge of safeguarding reconciliations, control frameworks, governance arrangements, and risk management processes.
• Ability to assess safeguarding risks, identify control deficiencies, and provide practical recommendations for remediation.
• Experience liaising with Compliance, Risk, Finance, and Operational stakeholders on CASS and safeguarding matters.
• Awareness of evolving FCA safeguarding regulations and industry developments within payments, e-money, and investment firms.
• You will ideally have one of the following professional qualifications – ACA, ACCA or CIMA
Knowing we’re right for you
Embracing uniqueness, the culture at Grant Thornton thrives on the contributions of all our people, we never settle for what is easy, we look beyond to deliver the right thing, for everyone.  Building an inclusive culture, where we value difference and respect our colleagues helps our people to perform at the best of their ability and realise their potential.
Our open and accessible culture means you’ll interact with leaders who are interested in you and everything you bring to our firm. The things that set you apart, we value them. That’s why we give you the freedom to bring your whole self to work and pursue your passions inside and outside of work.
Beyond the job
Life is more than work. The things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles, and we’ll always do our best to keep your work and life in balance.

Who We Are:
Since 1906, New Balance has empowered people through sport and craftsmanship to create positive change in communities around the world. We innovate fearlessly, guided by our core values and driven by the belief that conventions were meant to be challenged. We foster a culture in which every associate feels welcomed and respected, where leaders and creatives are inspired to shape the world of tomorrow by taking bold action today.
JOB MISSION:
The Senior Category Planning Manager, EMEA is the commercial planning lead for New Balance’s consumer performance and lifestyle categories. You will own the full seasonal planning cycle — from pre-season strategy to in-season trading and post-season hindsight — ensuring category ambition translates into commercial results across all EMEA channels and markets.
Sitting within the centralised EMEA Sales Planning function, you act as the bridge between Brand, Merchandising and the commercial organisation. You define how the category sells: building seasonal sales frameworks, investment logic, channel targets and in-season action plans that drive growth, healthy distribution and strong sell-through.
This role is ideal for someone who is highly analytical, commercially sharp and deeply connected to product, consumer and market.
MAJOR ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Lead Pre-Season Category Sales Planning
• Build and own the seasonal category sales plan for all EMEA channels: wholesale, DTC and e-commerce.
• Translate Brand and Merchandising priorities — key franchises, seasonal stories, range architecture — into clear commercial frameworks and revenue targets.
• Define option counts, depth-by-channel and investment levels to drive strong sell-in and healthy sell-through.
• Present and align plans with the Commercial Planning Director and senior commercial stakeholders, clearly articulating assumptions, risks and opportunities.
Drive Category Go-to-Market Execution
• Lead the Sales Planning contribution to the category GTM process from range sign-off to sell-in execution.
• Build seasonal sell-in toolkits: channel targets, assortment guidance and story prioritisation by account tier.
• Partner with Marketing to align sell-in plans with seasonal activation calendars and key consumer moments.
• Support market and account teams in sell-in preparation and coordinate allocation recommendations for constrained or launch product with Sales Planning and Supply Chain.
Manage In-Season Category Trading
• Own the in-season performance view across EMEA: weekly sell-through, inventory levels, reorders, best/slow sellers and markdown exposure.
• Identify risks and opportunities at category and franchise level and drive proactive commercial actions — reorders, stock rebalancing, exit strategies.
• Lead regular in-season category reviews with the Sales Planning Director and cross-functional partners.
• Work closely with market and account planning teams to resolve distribution health issues.
Build Category Intelligence & Consumer Insight
• Develop deep expertise in category dynamics: consumer profiles, seasonal demand patterns, franchise lifecycle, competitive positioning and market trends.
• Translate consumer insight and competitive intelligence into actionable commercial recommendations.
• Produce regular category market intelligence reports and contribute structured insight into global GTM and product creation processes.
Integrate Category Planning Across EMEA
• Act as the category planning authority within the central Sales Planning function.
• Ensure category dynamics are accurately reflected in the EMEA rolling forecast and annual commercial plan.
• Partner with Finance to align revenue and margin assumptions with EMEA financial targets.
• Build strong cross-functional relationships with Merchandising, Marketing, Customer Service and Supply Chain.
Support Market & Key Account Execution
• Ensure category plans translate effectively into market and account-level execution without compromising category strategy.
• Provide targeted support to key account teams on assortment recommendations, sell-through targets and in-season trading plans.
• Lead post-season hindsight reviews and translate learnings into improved frameworks for future seasons.
Talent and Team Development
• Develop and manage a small high-performing category planning team.
• Foster a culture of accountability, innovation and collaboration and across cross-functional partners.
REQUIREMENTS FOR SUCCESS:
• Experience in sales planning, category planning, assortment planning or commercial operations, ideally within sports, footwear or lifestyle.
• Strong understanding of category performance drivers: franchise lifecycle, assortment architecture, sell-through dynamics, inventory health and margin management.
• Highly analytical with advanced Excel skills; experience with BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, SAP, o9 or equivalent) preferred.
• Deep knowledge of seasonal GTM processes and experience partnering with Merchandising on assortment optimisation.
• Consumer-first mindset with strong product intuition and market awareness.
• Proven ability to collaborate across Sales, Merchandising, Marketing, Finance and Supply Chain in a matrix organisation.
• Experience managing, developing and leading a team.
• Confident communicator able to influence senior stakeholders.
• Solid understanding of the sporting goods and lifestyle retail landscape in EMEA.
• Degree in Business, Economics, Merchandising or related field.
• Fluent in English; additional European languages an advantage.
• Willingness to travel across EMEA for planning reviews, sales meetings and trade events.

• Discount on the health insurance

The Wellcome Trust is a politically and financially independent global charitable foundation dedicated to improving health through science. Established in 1936, it is funded entirely through returns from a £39.9bn investment portfolio, enabling a planned £16bn spend between 2022 and 2032 across discovery research, infectious disease, mental health, and climate and health.
Wellcome’s mission, a healthier future for all, is grounded in collaboration, diversity of expertise, and bold, high‑impact scientific ambition.
We are now seeking as part of succession planning to appoint a Governor to join our Board of Governors who would chair the Audit and Risk Committee. The Governor role is a senior non‑executive appointment on Wellcome’s Board of Governors, responsible for shaping long‑term strategy, safeguarding the endowment, and ensuring exemplary governance. Governors act as statutory directors of The Wellcome Trust Ltd., providing strategic oversight, setting risk appetite, holding leadership to account, and serving as ambassadors for Wellcome’s mission and its commitments to equity, diversity, anti‑racism, and inclusion.
Chair, Audit & Risk Committee
The ideal candidate will bring a mix of relevant commercial leadership, strategic acumen and board experience to contribute as a Governor across the board agenda, alongside financial expertise and the judgment and EQ to lead the Audit and Risk Committee.
Ideal Experience and Capabilities
• Global outlook with stature and judgement to operate in a high-profile governance environment.
• Strong financial expertise, whether gained as CFO or qualified accountant, or as a CEO and seasoned board member.
• Able to oversee complex risk, audit and investment governance issues and navigate potential conflicts.
• Brings credibility with business, finance, science and public-sector stakeholders.
• Strong communication skills and sophisticated interpersonal and social awareness to contribute effectively as a Governor and skillfully chair the committee.
• Demonstrates the capacity and commitment required for a demanding role.
• Independent thinker with the ability to challenge constructively and lead a strong committee.
How to apply
We have appointed the leadership advisory firm Spencer Stuart to lead the search for this position.
If you are interested in applying, please send your up-to-date CV and a supporting statement outlining your suitability for the role to: governorsapply@spencerstuart.com
Closing date for applications is Monday November 2nd.
You can view Spencer Stuart’s privacy policy here.
Please note any application submitted directly to Wellcome may not be considered.
Time Commitment
Wellcome anticipate a time commitment of approximately 35 days per year as a Governor and another 10 days to include the responsibility of chairing the committee.
There are typically four two-day meetings per year; a two-day strategic off-site meeting and an overseas visit, plus several other shorter online Board meetings.
Remuneration
Governors are appointed under a contract for services, which is currently remunerated at £80,500 per annum. Governors can claim reasonable expenses properly incurred for attending board meetings, such as travel, or on other Wellcome related business.
The appointments are for three years, requiring confirmation by the Board of Governors at the expiry of the first year. The appointments can be extended, by the board, by up to two additional terms of three years to a maximum of nine years.
Diversity and Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do
Diversity and Inclusion is a priority at Wellcome. We are committed to cultivating a fair and inclusive environment, where everyone can be themselves and thrive. This includes making adjustments for people who have a disability or long-term condition. Please visit our website for more information on adjustments and accessibility, or contact us at jobs@wellcome.org.
